loads._: What a calling carries in its arms where it isn't the move's own prop (weapons.gd LOADS; tools/carry_probe.gd): {calling (folk.role): {move: tool from weapons.gd TOOLS}}. The water carrier walks home from the well with a pail, not the basket every Carrying held.

_: The townsfolk's bodies and where they stand (people.gd reads it through data.gd; docs/TUNING.md). feet: every move stands on its feet (Unity's root height based upon feet): each clip's hips are raised by how far the lowest foot of its standing frames falls below the reference outfit's feet at rest. on: the switch (--feet=off for the clips' own keys); reference: the skeleton the clips are measured on; samples: poses measured per clip; mostLift: the most a clip or body is raised (metres, on a 0.95 m hip); seated: a frame with the hips under this share of their rest height is sat or lying and doesn't count; kneeling: nor one with a knee under this share of its rest height (on a knee). Crouches and lunges count. kneeRadius, instep: for a move that never stands (kneeling, praying, planting), how far the knee bone and a laid-down foot's bones stand above the ground (metres; seat: the hips' bone, sat back on the heels); it is raised by how far either goes under. bodyClips: the moves each Mixamo body's own legs are measured in, to raise the body by what its feet still fall short after the clips are planted on the reference. seats: moves (by the start of their name) sat on a cart's box or a saddle, kept as they are (sat on a bench or the ground, the feet still find the ground). low: each Mixamo body's low moves (motion.gd LOW, and lowAlso) are measured on its own skeleton and the body raised while one plays by what its knee, laid foot or seat still goes under the ground (fuse_civilian_1 sank 16 cm on a knee, the noble lady 14, the monk 13); lowExtra: metres more for a body, by its name, in every low move or by move ({clip: metres}). bodyMoves: standing moves measured the same way on each Mixamo body's own legs, and raised while they play by what its feet still fall short (a crouch's heel-up foot sank 10-12 cm on fuse_civilian_1 and Medieval Man). travel.groundStep: a road traveller's path takes its height from the ground this often (game units), not lerped between waypoints a tile apart.
_readable: readable (1.1 since Mac's steroids note, 2026-11-12; was 1.5; at 1.1 a man stands 0.235 units to the kit door's 0.214 at the houses' 0.85 scale): everyone drawn this much larger than life against the houses, as 01-town draws them (docs/review/look-gap.md: ours were 1.5-1.7x too small to read from the town view): people (people.gd READ), their beasts and horses (animals.gd, horse.gd), carts (scenes.gd, town_life.gd), with their stride (motion.gd), walking pace (villagers.gd, the square's walkers) and the room they keep from each other and from walls (town_life.gd ROOM, CLEAR). 1.0 is life size.
_held: held: what's in a hand (weapons.gd: swords, spears, bows, shields, hammers, baskets, pails) drawn this much larger again, from the grip (quality-deep-dive.md #9: tools and weapons read at the town view at about 1.3 over the bodies' scale).
_build: build (Mac 2026-11-12: the NPCs on steroids at 1.5x): female, a woman's height against a man's; slim_cast, a Meshy cast body narrowed across (x and z) on its skeleton (its upper arms stood 26% of its height apart, a man's are about 20%); slim_kit the same for the kit bodies. 1.0 leaves them as made.
_dress: dress (the supervisor's dress code, 12 Nov; people.gd _tabard, _gold_belt): tabard, the watch's livery over the house-coloured tunic: a panel down the chest (panel colour; width: share of the chest's half width either side; tall: its height to its width; drop: how far below the chest bone, share of its height; out: metres off the chest's front, read off the body's own vertices within band metres of the bone) with the house's sigil on it in the house's colour (arms: its size to the panel's width), the house found by its colour among the realm's houses. gold: a merchant's or a gentlewoman's gold belt at the waist (colour, fit: its radius to the waist's, thick metres, up: metres above the hips bone). on: off for none.
_proportions: proportions: what tools/proportion_probe.gd holds the crowd to, against 01-town: a child's head height as a share of a grown man's [lowest, highest] (01-town's children stand about 0.6 of a man), a woman's, and a man's head against the kit door's top (never taller than his doors). dress: what tools/dress_probe.gd holds the crown's square to (01-town counted 2026-11-12: of about 27 townsfolk some 16 in crimson, one in blue, none in green, two of three children in red): the red share [lowest, highest] and the most of blue and green together; nobody in pink. To get there the dyes lost their green, one blue and a third cream to crimson, brick and madder red, the rich lost a blue and the green to deep reds, the children's linen took two reds, and the crown's town wears its house's colour at 0.3 (was 0.2): before 0.31 red, 0.19 blue and green. build.ages sets the heights by age (child 0.62, was 0.72 in code: the probe measured 0.70, out of its range).
_rise: rise: how someone gets up from a low move (npc_mind.gd GetUp; Mac's clip 2026-11-12: Getting_Up, Mixamo's rise from lying flat on the back, played after every sit and kneel, read as a body on the cobbles with its legs in the air). on: off for Getting_Up after every low move, as before. lying: the moves that leave them on their back, risen from with from_lying; seated: the moves on a bench or seat, risen from with from_seat; any other low move (a kneel, a seat on the ground) has no rise, the next move blends them up.
_steer: steer (Mac 2026-11-12: 'there isn't gradual smooth actions'): how townsfolk walk and turn (villagers.gd _step, npc_mind Turn). on: the switch (--steer=off: the old snap turns and full-pace starts and stops). turn: how fast they turn, radians a second, walking or on the spot (turn_min: the shortest turn on the spot, seconds); turn_slow: the least of their pace kept while facing well off their way (a sharp turn made mostly on the spot, no sliding sideways); start: seconds to ease up to pace from a standstill, from start_from of it; arrive: game units from the end over which they ease down, to arrive_from of their pace; smooth: how quickly their heading follows the avoidance's nudges (higher, quicker); corner: how far before a waypoint on the way they make for the next (the path bends round corners). xfade: seconds every change of move blends over (motion.gd XFADE, was 0.2). turn_clips: Mixamo's turn-in-place clips, their hips' yaw taken out at load (people.gd _unturn), played for a turn on the spot of more than turn_clip_over degrees, the turn taking turn_clip_share of the clip's length (the research's 'turn before you walk').
_furniture: furniture: what people sit on, eat at and work at, drawn at their size (readable) so the drinkers sit on the benches and not proud of them (town_life.gd _prop: the inn's benches, the long tables and what's set on them, the anvils; the benches 0.53 m and tables 0.81 m high at life size). on: the switch (--furniture=off draws them life size); props: the kit's names that grow.
_cloth: What the crowd wears (people.gd cloth_pick; batch 8 look2: dark, colourless clothes against town-b's warm, varied crowd). homespun: the undyed wool and linen a peasant wears; dyed: the colours the dyers sell (madder, woad, weld, greens, cream, russet, plum, saffron). rank: by the town's rank, the share of peasants who wear dyed cloth (dyed) and the share of everyone who wears the holder's colour (house; house_soften: how much paler than his banner). mourning: what a town in grief wears (dark wool: black, ash, charcoal), worn by all of it. true: cloth dyed in its true colour on its weave (its own colour taken out, the weave lifted to a mean brightness of weave), not multiplied onto the cloth's own colour, which came out dark and muddy. 2026-11-12, look-gap.md: 01-town dresses its townsfolk in reds, creams and whites and ochres, ours wore blue-grey and brown; the dyes are now mostly reds, whites and ochres with one green and one soft blue, the homespun lighter, and the crown's town wears more dye and more of its house's colour. cast_dye (round 3: the crowd read grey-brown against 01-town's bright reds, whites, yellows and blues): how a Meshy cast member's masked cloth takes its dye; mode mix lays the dye over the painted cloth at strength (mul, the switch back, multiplied it in and darkened it), lift brightens the whole figure, skin too; livery_strength: a soldier's house colour, laid on near whole (round 4: red at 0.72 over the guard's pale leather read pink); the salmon dye dropped (it read pink). The dyes gained a clear blue and a saffron yellow, the green and blue brighter, and the crown's town wears dye on 85% of its peasants (was 70%). Round 8 (everyone red: 54% of a crowd of 80 counted headless): the crown's townsfolk wear the house's colour less (rank.crown.house 0.16, was 0.32; the guards keep the full livery), one of the two deep reds dropped, a walnut brown and a linen white added: reds, whites, yellows, blues and browns as 01-town mixes them. Dress code (the supervisor, 12 Nov; product call logged): townsfolk in the town's dyes with the house's colour only now and then (rank house, the crown's 0.2, about one in five: a cast body takes the dye on its one garment, so the accent is a whole garment, never a sash: our masks dye one cloth); the watch and castle folk in full livery (livery_strength); merchants and gentlewomen from palettes.rich (deep green, blue, burgundy); children from palettes.child (undyed linen, browns). Which cast member wears which palette: cast.json palette.
_seen_to: seen_to: world units beyond which a person isn't drawn or animated (a few pixels tall). near_fade: within gone of the lens a person is gone, beyond solid fully there (about 0.7 m and 1.5 m).

motion._: How a body moves between its clips (motion.gd): xfade_hit, seconds into a blow, a reel or a fall; settle, seconds moving or still before a standing move gives way or comes back; xfade_stand, seconds between two standing moves; turn_ease, how quickly a turn settles (per second); step_floor and step_ceil, the slowest and quickest cadence a moving walk plays at, of its own speed (past step_ceil it breaks into the run).
